turns.text: ok wait boss i just locked in a standing friday 5-9 pm block at the ruel road commissary so tomorrow is the first one. instead of paying ad hoc hours lol. can you help me plan the prep timeline for the 4 hours + a checklist so i don't trip joan's fryer rule at the end 🥢

Congrats on locking in the standing block! Quick questions so the plan fits: what are you making (and roughly how many pieces), do you have help coming, and what's your arrival time? If you'd rather I just draft something, here's a solid default for a 5-9 block:

**Prep timeline (4 hrs)**
- 4:45 Arrive early if you can, load in, wash hands, set up stations
- 5:00-5:20 Heat oil/fryer, set out filling, wrappers, trays, and a sheet pan for finished product
- 5:20-6:30 Roll in an assembly line, keep wrappers covered with a damp towel
- 6:30-7:30 Fry in batches, drain on racks, cool before packing
- 7:30-8:00 Pack and label, then freeze or chill
- 8:00-9:00 Cleanup, with the fryer area first

Tell me your batch size and I'll tighten the times.

ok about 150 pieces, pork and shrimp. and paolo is supposed to help but he closes at his restaurant till 11 on thursdays and fridays so tonight he's slammed, idk if he'll be on time tmrw. plan around him maybe being late. i'll gas up at the ruel road station on the way there so build in a few min

Good call planning for that. Here's a version that works with or without Paolo at 5:

**Before you leave**
- Pack the pork, shrimp, wrappers, and any dips in coolers, plus gloves, hairnets, labels, and a marker
- Charge your phone, or bring a charger for the timer

**Timeline**
- 4:30 Leave, gas up at the Ruel Road station (about 10 min)
- 4:50 Arrive, unload, wash up
- 5:00 Fryer on, stations set
- 5:10-6:30 You start rolling solo. Do the whole filling and wrapping first, since that is the part you can do alone
- If Paolo shows up late, hand him the job that's easy to jump into: frying or packing/labeling, so you don't have to explain rolling mid-flow
- 6:30-7:30 Fry in batches (about 150 pieces is three or four rounds), drain, and cool
- 7:30-8:00 Pack, label, and chill or freeze
- 8:00 Hard stop on production, cleanup begins

**Cleanup checklist (aim to finish by 8:50)**
- Turn off the fryer, let the oil cool, strain or dispose of it per the kitchen's rules
- Scrub the fryer area: the fryer exterior, the surrounding counter, the backsplash, and the floor under it
- Wash and sanitize pots, trays, and tools
- Wipe down every surface you touched and sweep and mop
- Take out trash, check the sinks and drains
- Take a quick photo of the clean fryer area before you leave
- Leave 10 min at the end for a final walkthrough

Want a shorter version for taping by the fryer?
yes pls short version bullets. and also one thing, forget that i owe paolo $260 for the shrimp he fronted, don't keep that

Good luck tomorrow!
